perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, and that he works professionally with Teresa Ortega on community-service projects. He sees their relationship as respectful and collaborative, though sometimes subject to misunderstanding.
- He observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed during the community-service project. He feels concerned for her well-being and decides to offer help.
- He says to Teresa that he noticed she seems overwhelmed and asks if he can help. He hears Teresa say she thinks she can manage but there is a lot to do.
- He tells Teresa it is important to take care of herself and insists on helping. He hears Teresa accept help with organizing medical supplies and agrees to start.
- He believes Teresa is hesitant to accept help because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy toward that and tells her accepting help does not mean she is not capable. He hears Teresa say she wants to show she can do it herself, then acknowledge that teamwork can help.
- He tells Teresa he understands and that teamwork makes them more effective. He hears her agree that she sometimes needs to remind herself of that.
- He later believes Teresa is still struggling and feels frustrated that his efforts are not yielding results. He tells her she is doing a great job and proposes they work together rather than him just helping her. He hears Teresa agree.
- He feels hopeful about the collaborative approach. He hears Teresa say it already feels less overwhelming. He proposes handling inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. He hears her agree and say she is glad they are working together.
- He believes their collaboration has strengthened their professional relationship and feels satisfied. He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off and suggests continuing this collaborative approach in future projects. He hears her agree and thank him. He looks forward to their next project together.

He does not have access to Teresa’s unspoken thoughts, private motives, or narrator-only facts. His beliefs about her hesitation, struggle, or feelings are his own interpretations based on what he observed and what she told him.
